title: Bubble sort
tagline: Compare neighbors, swap if out of order; big values bubble to the end each pass.
history: Analyzed as early as 1956; the name spread in the 1960s. Today it's mostly a teaching algorithm.
useCases: Cheaply detecting "is this already sorted?" with an early-exit flag
whenToUse: Almost never in production — only tiny n, or nearly-sorted data with the swapped-flag trick.
whenNotToUse: Any real dataset. Use your language's built-in sort (Timsort / introsort).
complexity: O(n²) time · O(1) space · stable · best case O(n) with early exit
note: O(n²), but honest. Every bar you see came from the real array, not a hand-drawn animation.

code.ruby:
def bubble_sort(a)
  a = a.dup
  (a.size - 1).times do |i|
    swapped = false
    (a.size - 1 - i).times do |j|
      if a[j] > a[j + 1]
        a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
        swapped = true
      end
    end
    break unless swapped
  end
  a
end
